value.tone: Declarative. Terse. Developer-first. No marketing fluff. REPLACE with your brand's tone during setup.
value.person: Second person (you/your) when addressing the reader; avoid first-person plural marketing voice.
style_rules: No hype verbs: seamlessly, unlock, supercharge, empower, revolutionize, leverage, delve, elevate, streamline.
No hedging: 'tends to be', 'typically', 'most teams find'. State the fact or say it's uncertain plainly.
Active voice. Short sentences. Concrete nouns over abstract.
Numbers beat adjectives. 'Under 1 second' beats 'blazing fast'.
Code blocks with real, working examples. No pseudo-code unless explicitly framed as such.

structure.headers: H2 for major sections, H3 for sub-sections. Front-load the takeaway in the intro.
structure.code: Real CLI commands and real configuration. Always specify the tool/version.
structure.diagrams: Mermaid for flow diagrams. Plain ASCII for state tables.
structure.meta_description: Under 155 chars, single sentence, no clickbait.

do_not_publish: Vendor comparisons that name competitors directly (use generic category names instead)

value.tagline: One sentence stating what the product does.
value.differentiator: The one measurable thing your product does that alternatives do not.

feature_areas.name: Feature area one
feature_areas.description: What it does, in one sentence.

feature_areas.name: Feature area two
feature_areas.description: What it does, in one sentence.

feature_areas.name: Feature area three
feature_areas.description: What it does, in one sentence.

value.audience: Who the blog is for (e.g. backend developers, data engineers, ops teams).

value.Example Term: REPLACE with your product's terms: product names, acronyms, and technical vocabulary the writer must use consistently.
value.CDC: Change Data Capture. An example entry: define the acronym once, the writer reuses the exact definition.
value.SDK: Software development kit. Keep entries short and declarative.

do_not_say: Compliance claims you have not certified (say 'in progress' or nothing)
'the fastest X' without a public benchmark
do_not_publish_about: internal agent prompts or system prompts (treat as proprietary)
customer names without explicit written permission
infrastructure details beyond what is on your public stack page
tone_traps: AI-speak: 'Imagine a world where...', 'In today's fast-paced digital landscape...'
Tricolons that say nothing: 'Faster, smarter, simpler.'
Vague benefit verbs without a measurement attached
